title: Fine-Grained Policy Orchestrator: Segment-Based Routing, Route Allow/Deny Controls, and Safe Auto-Apply
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an orchestrator that applies cost-optimization policies (adaptive batching and prefix/KV caching) at per-customer and per-route granularity using segments and allow/deny controls, plus a hardened safe-apply and rollback system for automated configuration changes.

Goals:
- Allow operators and PMs to define segmentation rules (by customer ID, route, model, and traffic signal) that map to a policy bundle: batching strategy, cache TTLs, quantization hint, and cost target.
- Support allowlists and denylists at the route-level and customer-level to prevent unsafe optimization (e.g., low-latency paid routes) from receiving aggressive batching/caching.
- Provide an automated apply pipeline that runs staged checks (synthetic traffic sims + perf regressions) and executes canary rollout with automatic rollback on violations.
- Expose controls in Console and API to preview effective policy for a given customer+route.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement new kernel-level batching primitives; it reuses the runtime batching interface.
- Not covering multi-tenant sidecar deployment changes for Private on-prem (follow-up).

Design overview:
- Policy model: a policy bundle is a named set of knobs: max_batch_ms, target_batch_size, prefix_cache_ttl_ms, kv_cache_policy (none|per-route|per-customer), quantization_profile, priority_override, and fallbacks. Policies are bound via SegmentRules. SegmentRules are evaluated in order and contain matcher expressions (customer_id regex, route tag, model family).
- Allow/Deny semantics: Deny rules short-circuit policy application and force "opt-out" behavior (no batching beyond baseline, no caching). Allow rules opt-in and have higher precedence when explicitly set. Admins can mark routes as "sensitive" to enforce deny-by-default.
- Safe-apply pipeline: changes submitted to the policy store trigger a preflight job: (1) static validation, (2) simulation using representative traffic profiles (from saved clusters), (3) dark-canary where new policy is executed against copy of runtime but responses are not returned, (4) staged live canary rollout (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with metric checks.
- Automatic rollback criteria: increase in 99th latency > 15% absolute, failure rate > 0.5% increase, output-quality regression on eval prompts (BLEU/ROUGE-like threshold or custom prompt set drift), or cost savings below expected threshold while degrading latency. Thresholds are configurable per project.
- Observability: policy-level metrics (cost delta, batching efficiency, cache hit rate, P50/P95/P99 latency), per-segment dashboards, and alerts. All policy decisions should be traceable in request spans (policy_id, rule_match, applied_knobs).

APIs & Console:
- New REST endpoints: POST /policies, GET /policies/{id}/preview?customer=..., POST /policies/{id}/apply (with dry_run=true), POST /policies/{id}/rollback.
- Console: policy editor with rule simulator, preview panel (sample requests show what would be applied), canary control slider, manual rollback button, and audit log.

Safety notes and trade-offs considered:
- Trade-off: tighter batching reduces cost but increases tail latency. We opt for per-segment SLO checks and conservative defaults for paid or sensitive routes.
- Trade-off: fuller automation speeds ops but increases blast radius. Mitigation: staged rollout, dark-canary, and hard-deny labels for critical routes.

Operational plan:
- Phase 1 (MVP): policy model, store, preview API, static validation, and dark-canary runner. Manual triggering of staged rollout.
- Phase 2: automated staged rollout with metric guards and auto-rollback. Console UX and dashboarding.
- Phase 3: cross-region replication, support for Private deployments, and integration with Optimize recommendations engine (auto-suggest policies).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Policy can be created, validated, and previewed for arbitrary customer+route.
2) Dark-canary executes against saved runtime snapshot and emits policy traces without impacting production responses.
3) Canary rollout supports percentage gating and enforces all automatic rollback criteria when triggered in e2e tests.
4) Console shows per-policy cost delta and latency impact after canary.
5) Audit logs capture who applied changes, what changed, and timestamps.

Manual rollback steps (backstop):
1) Console -> Policy -> Rollback -> trigger immediate rollback to previous policy id and force-disable new policy across route.
2) If console rollback fails, call /policies/{id}/rollback-rest API which writes a high-priority override to the routing layer.
3) On-call runbook: revert feature-flag + redeploy latest policy agent.

Notes: This ticket requires coordination with Runtime team to ensure policy traces are emitted and with Console team for editor components. Also requires Security review (KMS usage for policy signing) and Privacy review for any stored traffic used in sims.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Policies created via API and Console. 2) Preview endpoint returns deterministic effective policy for sample input. 3) Dark-canary produces traces without returning responses. 4) Staged canary can be executed manually and auto-rolls back on defined thresholds. 5) Console displays cost and latency delta post-canary.
